title: A Look at Hero’s Journey Home
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iCrYuW2ixu8

The game that ships in a burlap sack. Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at Graham Cranfield's *Hero's Journey Home*, a one-man operation — design, art, packaging and shipping all by the same hands.

The premise inverts the usual structure: your quest is already complete, and the game is the walk back. You draw which quest you finished — the Minotaur, Baba Yaga, the Cockatrice of Werel, the Devil himself — and that determines both your trophy item and the point budget for assembling your party. Heroes carry intrinsic abilities that are always active and extrinsic ones spent as actions. Spellcasters draw their spells at random from the deck, and casting is paid in paper gold, the same currency used to bribe monsters and buy gear.

Structurally it is a deck you work down until you draw the home card, shuffled into the bottom half. Combat cross-references attacker and defender strength on a chart for a d20 target. Your other adventurers are frankly meat shields; only the hero must survive. The *Gods of Man* expansion adds a deity per hero and optional race cards that mostly make things harder.

Daniel is candid that he likes this game chiefly for how it looks — whimsical, Gorey-by-way-of-Burton, genuinely inviting on the table. He'd like a variant laying cards out as a grid to travel rather than a straight deck.

----

A game loved mostly for how it looks on the table, by Daniel's own admission. Does that count as a good game?
